Building internal capabilities is crucial to continuing the ESG journey. In addition to encouraging staff to undertake sustainability-related courses and obtain relevant qualifications, the HKMA has also drawn on knowledge and practical experience gained through the process of engaging external consultants since 2021 to provide advice on key industry practices for portfolio climate transition. Furthermore, the HKMA leverages ESG data compiled by reputable external data providers to supplement its ongoing portfolio analysis, helping to strengthen the Exchange Fund's ESG resilience.

The HKMA is committed to reducing its own carbon footprint, with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, and contributing to Hong Kong's overall climate targets. While striving to promote environmental sustainability, the HKMA also fulfils its commitments to staff well-being, financial inclusion, and social responsibility. The HKMA is committed to conducting its daily operations in a responsible and sustainable manner. To this end, the HKMA implements its sustainability philosophy under three pillars: environment, staff, and social responsibility (Diagram 1). The Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee is responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating and implementing its sustainability strategy. The Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with members comprising three Deputy Chief Executives and representatives from the Risk Management and Oversight Department and the Corporate Development and Operations Department; it submits regular reports to the Governance Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee. Under the guidance of the Committee, various teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing measures within their respective areas. In 2022, the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee approved climate targets for institutional operations and reviewed the transition roadmap for achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. During the year, the Committee continued to review progress on the HKMA's green initiatives, including proposals to strengthen the HKMA's sustainable procurement policies, procedures, and methodologies.  Sustainability Governance Framework HKMA's Corporate Sustainability Journey In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to caring for the environment, staff, and the broader community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service presented the HKMA with the "15 Years+ Caring Organisation" logo for the 16th consecutive year.  The HKMA pays close attention to its own carbon footprint and has established internal Green Office Guidelines to manage the environmental impact of its operational processes. The HKMA has incorporated environmental considerations into the interior design, operations, and maintenance of its offices. In 2022, BEAM Plus awarded the HKMA Gold certification for certain renovated office areas. This was the second green building certification received, following the Gold certification awarded by LEED in 2021.  BEAM Plus Interior Buildings Version 1.0 Gold Award  The HKMA implements a number of energy-saving measures. Total energy consumption in 2022 was 4,996.4 MWh (2.8 MWh per person), a decrease of 24.4% compared with 2015 (Figure 1). Total Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions in 2022 amounted to 2,996.4 tonnes of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e) (1.7 tCO2e per person), a reduction of 38.2% compared with 2015 (Figure 2).  Figure 1 Figure 2: Greenhouse Gas Emissions Intensity (Scope 1 and 2)  The HKMA encourages paperless internal operations. In addition, the HKMA has implemented a print management system whereby staff must log in to printers to confirm each print job, helping to reduce unnecessary printouts and toner usage. Where printing is genuinely necessary, double-sided printing and black-and-white printing are encouraged. The HKMA is also preparing to implement an internal electronic records management system. Total paper consumption in 2022 was 20.5 tonnes (0.0114 tonnes per person), a reduction of 65.3% compared with 2015 (Figure A).  Figure A: Paper Consumption Intensity  The HKMA's waste management efforts continue to follow the "4R" principle. In addition to conventional waste, the HKMA reduces electronic waste through the adoption of technological solutions such as server virtualisation and private cloud infrastructure. In 2022, the HKMA engaged an external company to conduct a waste audit for the first time to analyse the composition of waste generated in the office. The audit found that food waste constituted a significant proportion of total waste, prompting the HKMA to launch a food waste recycling programme (see "Enhancing Waste Management" on page 41). Total non-hazardous waste generated in 2022 (including general waste and recyclable waste) was 242.0 tonnes (0.135 tonnes per person), a decrease of 4.8% compared with 2015 (Figure 3). Fluctuations in the trend were mainly attributable to work-from-home arrangements during peak COVID-19 periods and the resumption of office operations following the fifth wave.  Figure 3: Non-Hazardous Waste Intensity  The HKMA places waste reduction at source as the top priority and is committed to reducing, reusing, and recycling. In 2022, the HKMA engaged a company to conduct a waste audit for the first time to better understand the composition of waste generated in daily operations (plastics, paper, metals, glass, wood, electronics, etc.) and to receive waste reduction recommendations. Based on the findings of the audit, the HKMA launched a food waste recycling programme in November, placing food waste collection bins in all pantries. Food waste collected daily is transported to an organic waste treatment facility in Hong Kong, where it is converted into renewable energy for electricity generation. The residual matter produced during the process can also be made into compost for use in landscaping and agricultural staple food production. Additionally, recycling bins are conveniently located at various points throughout the office. The HKMA shares recycling tips with staff and pays greater attention to improving source separation of recyclables, as well as the proper handling of recyclable items such as cardboard boxes, food containers, and beverage bottles. We also continue to organise activities to raise staff environmental awareness, explain waste management policies, and encourage staff to make good use of the recycling facilities in the office.  Food waste collected daily transported to organic waste treatment facility Recycling plastic items  The HKMA operates two data centres (production and backup). As these account for a significant proportion of the organisation's overall energy consumption, the HKMA has adopted green design and various energy-saving measures, including in-row cooling systems, LED lighting, and round-the-clock monitoring of power usage effectiveness. Following the completion of a consultancy study on the green performance of these data centres in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations to improve overall energy efficiency. Preparations have also commenced for obtaining green data centre certification.  The HKMA recognises the importance of building a culture of sustainability, and therefore regularly introduces various programmes and activities to educate and encourage staff to adopt sustainable habits and green and digital ways of working. The HKMA shares green living tips with staff, along with annual office-wide energy consumption and paper usage statistics, to remind them to help address environmental issues at the individual level; staff are also encouraged to put forward suggestions on sustainability matters. Under the leadership of a Senior Manager in the Administration Division, a thematic group brings together staff from different departments to pool ideas and propose initiatives for promoting a green working environment. Members of the thematic group also serve as ambassadors when new green initiatives are launched.  The HKMA encourages the broader community to adopt more environmentally friendly practices and has introduced various measures to enhance the operational efficiency of the HKMA, the financial industry, and the wider economy, with a view to minimising resource consumption. The HKMA's Electronic Transmission Return System (STET) is a one-stop platform for banks to submit documents electronically to the HKMA, covering various types of periodic returns required on a weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annual basis. Another system, the Electronic Delivery System (e-Delivery), is a secure electronic communication channel through which the HKMA disseminates information such as circulars and guidelines to banks. Both systems help save a significant amount of paper each year.  In handling bank complaints and enforcement work, the HKMA has taken steps to support paperless submission of documents, allowing bank customers to lodge complaints through electronic channels and by completing online forms. The HKMA is also developing a new-generation management information system to facilitate complaint handling and the transition from paper-based records to digital records.  To reduce paper usage, the CMU has adopted digital signatures in its day-to-day communications with participants, including the issuance of circulars, account opening and closing letters, and responses to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, the CMU will continue to explore further green measures, including the adoption of automated electronic processes for internal and external communications.  The HKMA encourages greater adoption of electronic payments in place of cash and physical cheques by promoting the use of the faster payment systems "FPS" and stored value payment instruments. Further information on FPS and stored value payment instruments is contained in the chapter on "Hong Kong as International Financial Centre" in the HKMA's 2022 Annual Report.  Sending electronic red packets is simple and convenient, and reduces the use of physical red packet envelopes and banknotes, contributing to sustainable development in Hong Kong. To this end, the HKMA has continued to actively promote the practice on various social media and traditional platforms, encouraging members of the public to send electronic red packets via online or mobile banking services using FPS or other e-wallet services during the Lunar New Year period. Banks and e-wallet operators have also organised various activities to attract users to adopt electronic red packets, such as offering festive user interfaces, enhancing features to improve convenience, and launching lucky draws or cashback offers.  The HKMA promotes electronic red packets on social media platforms.  For members of the public who prefer to give physical red packets during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continues to encourage the use of "fit notes" — banknotes that, while not new, remain in good condition — for use in red packets. Fit notes reduce the need to print new banknotes, thereby lessening the environmental impact. Feedback from note-issuing banks indicates that public acceptance of fit notes has increased in recent years.  The Coin Collection Programme reflects the HKMA's efforts in promoting coin recycling. Coins collected through the programme are returned to circulation to meet public demand, improving the efficiency of coin circulation and reducing the need for minting. The programme operates two coin collection vehicles, which to date have served over one million people and collected more than 800 million coins with a total face value of approximately HKD 1.3 billion. In 2022, approximately 78% of users chose to add some or all of the value of their coins to stored value payment instrument accounts.  The HKMA has maintained its collaboration with the Hong Kong Council of Social Service, deploying coin collection vehicles at flag days organised by non-governmental organisations to provide support for social services.  Coin counting machines on the coin collection vehicles.  The Coin Collection Programme, launched in 2014, was the world's first systematic coin collection programme to adopt the concept of mobile vehicles. Over the years, it has received numerous local and international awards in recognition of its innovative and environmentally friendly approach to coin handling. The programme operates two coin collection vehicles, each equipped with two high-speed coin counting machines to collect coins exchanged by the public. Members of the public may choose to exchange their coins for banknotes, add the value to stored value payment instrument (such as Octopus Card or e-wallet) accounts, or donate the proceeds to the Community Chest as charitable contributions. In addition to coin collection, the coin collection vehicles are also deployed from time to time for various educational activities, such as student visits.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) has conducted an independent verification of the climate targets (the "Climate Targets") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The Climate Targets were developed with reference to the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual (the "SBTi Corporate Manual"). The purpose of this verification exercise is to verify whether the Climate Targets have been set with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. This verification exercise was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to provide a reasonable level of assurance for forming an opinion and conclusion. The verification process was carried out in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of data. Our verification work is completely independent and impartial. Based on the results of this verification, the HKQAA provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: • The Climate Targets have been set with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. Shen Xiaoyin, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023  Verification Statement  The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) has conducted an independent verification of the 2022 Environmental Data (the "2022 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The 2022 Data includes the total energy consumption in 2022, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emission intensity, paper consumption intensity, non-hazardous waste generation intensity and recycling rate in 2022, as well as changes in these data compared to 2015 levels. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the "GHG Protocol") jointly published by the World Resources Institute (the "WRI") and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (the "WBCSD"). The scope of verification covers relevant data for the period from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2022, as well as relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison. The verification scope covers a total of 6 office and warehouse asset, with 4 offices located at 1) Two International financial centres, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Pacific Place One, and 4) Landmark East, and 2 warehouses at 5) Melody Industrial Centre and 6) Chung Lee Centre, located in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan respectively. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, the HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from 6 asset. This verification exercise was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to provide a reasonable level of assurance for forming an opinion and conclusion. The verification process was carried out in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checking, and conducted reliability testing. The verification process also included verifying internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 Data, and selecting representative data and information for checking. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also subject to detailed review during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of data. Our verification work is completely independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the preparation of the 2022 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the HKQAA provides reasonable assurance on the 2022 Data and concludes that: • The 2022 Data are materially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023

Scaling up and accelerating climate action has become the most pressing challenge of our time. We are almost halfway through the critical decade for addressing the climate crisis. We need to reduce global carbon emissions by more than 40% during this decade to have any hope of keeping global warming within 1.5 degrees Celsius. Yet greenhouse gas emissions continue to reach new highs. The latest climate science indicates that the window for limiting global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius will close very soon. The impacts of a 1.1-degree rise in temperature are already being felt acutely — record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding and storms, and other extreme weather events are occurring with increasing frequency and intensity around the world. Hong Kong is no exception. Last September, we experienced a ferocious super typhoon, followed immediately by a once-in-a-century rainstorm. Despite our robust infrastructure and rapid emergency response capabilities, the impact was severe — widespread flooding, traffic disruptions, and road damage across many areas. All of this serves as a stark reminder that decisive and proactive climate action is urgently needed.  Asia faces particularly significant challenges on the path to low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development with sustainability. We need credible transition strategies that appropriately balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means easy. Given the region's rapid economic development and fast-growing population, its carbon emissions account for more than half of global total emissions. At the same time, the Asia Pacific region, with its high population density and geographical characteristics, is also highly vulnerable to rising sea levels and extreme weather events. Given the varying stages of development among regional economies, while the low-carbon transition will bring new opportunities for some, financing the transition poses enormous challenges for others. Market estimates suggest that the Asia Pacific region will require more than US$3 trillion per year in low-carbon transition investment over the next 30 years. As an international financial centre, Hong Kong has both the capacity and the responsibility to harness the power of finance to support the low-carbon transition across Asia.  As a banking regulator, market facilitator, and responsible investor, the HKMA has been making significant efforts on the sustainability agenda. Readers will find details of the various specific measures and initiatives introduced by the HKMA over the past year in the respective chapters of this report. In addition, to strengthen the HKMA's internal governance structure and better coordinate sustainability work across different functional areas, we established a Green and Sustainable Steering Committee last year. Details of this Steering Committee can be found in the new "Governance of Sustainability" chapter.  Hong Kong's banking sector plays a vital role in supporting Asia's transition to net zero. Beyond fulfilling our traditional role as a banking regulator — ensuring that banks properly manage climate risk in our day-to-day supervisory work — we also act as a facilitator to support the banking sector in financing the low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a green taxonomy framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched a prototype green taxonomy framework for consultation in May and are currently refining the framework based on feedback received during the consultation period. Furthermore, as demand grows for higher-quality and globally comparable sustainability disclosure information, the HKMA is working with other regulators to develop a clear roadmap for Hong Kong to adopt the disclosure standards issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board in June — a comprehensive set of global sustainability reporting common baselines.  The HKMA's role as a facilitator goes beyond setting frameworks and rules; we are also committed to addressing pain points faced by the industry. Many banks currently face data constraints that make physical risk assessment difficult. In response, the HKMA will shortly launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform. By simply entering property addresses, banks will be able to assess the impact of physical hazards on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios, thereby helping banks manage related climate risk.  As a major international financial centre and sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong has been playing a bridging role, channelling international investment into sustainable development projects across Asia and supporting the region's low-carbon transition. In recent years, international green and sustainable bonds arranged in Hong Kong have accounted for more than one-third of the Asian market, significantly ahead of other regions. Particularly noteworthy is the fact that the Shenzhen Municipal Government and the Hainan Provincial Government issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong for the third and second consecutive years respectively in 2023, reaffirming Hong Kong's important role as a green gateway connecting the Mainland with the rest of the world.  Hong Kong's sustainable bond activity has flourished in part due to the demonstration effect of the Government Green Bond Programme. Since 2019, the HKMA has helped the Government issue approximately US$25 billion worth of green bonds to institutional and retail investors. We have seized every issuance opportunity to innovate and expand the features of green bonds — including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels — laying the groundwork for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world's largest government retail green bonds in 2022, we issued the world's first tokenised green bond by a government in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed our second issuance of tokenised green bonds; denominated in four major currencies and issued in digital native form, these were the world's first multi-currency digital green bond.  At the same time, we have proactively introduced various measures to enhance the vibrancy and competitiveness of Hong Kong's sustainable finance ecosystem. This encompasses work across multiple areas including skills training, data improvement, green fintech, and transition finance. In particular, on talent development, we introduced a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for the banking sector in 2023, providing practitioners with a structured curriculum to enhance their knowledge and expertise in green and sustainable finance.  Transition finance is another key area of focus for us. It provides funding for decarbonisation activities in high-emission and hard-to-abate sectors, preventing these industries from failing to transition due to lack of financial support. To support the sound development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand Hong Kong's green taxonomy framework to cover transition activities. We will also expand the coverage of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme — which provides subsidies to eligible bond issuers and borrowers — to include transition bonds and loans, encouraging regional enterprises to raise transition financing in Hong Kong. In addition, we will strengthen engagement with relevant stakeholders and leverage public-private partnerships and blended finance models to attract private sector investment into sustainable development projects that have historically had difficulty accessing financing.  Some of the above work requires cross-sector collaboration and is coordinated primarily through the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional cooperation is equally important. In addition to our long-standing collaboration with the International Finance Corporation on the "Green Commercial Banking Alliance," the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the "Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance" and the "Partnership for Green Development Investment and Financing" as founding members in 2023. Furthermore, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero announced plans to establish a chapter in Hong Kong. Through these partnerships, we aim to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, thereby supporting the channelling of capital into sustainable development projects across the region and around the world.  To drive new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA also helped organise the inaugural "Hong Kong Green Week" earlier this year, attracting more than 1,600 participants from nearly 30 regions — including top decision-makers from the global business and financial community — to discuss ways to scale up climate finance in the region and forge new partnerships. HKMA Chief Executive Mr Eddie Yue delivered a speech at the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum," the flagship event of Hong Kong Green Week.  As the manager of Hong Kong's official reserves and a significant global asset owner, the HKMA leads by example as a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been pioneering investment in green and sustainable assets, progressively expanding the Exchange Fund's ESG and green asset portfolio in both public and private markets. In pursuit of the goal of achieving net zero emissions in the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, the HKMA last year added an actively managed global equity portfolio themed around sustainability and climate transition, while also extending the application of customised low-carbon equity indices to another public market asset portfolio. In addition, the HKMA's prioritised investments in green, social, and sustainable bonds have outperformed investment benchmarks, demonstrating the proposition of "doing good while doing well."  In private markets, we continue to seek green-related investment opportunities and have become an anchor investor in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. By end-2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio had decreased by 6% and 46% compared with 2021 and 2017 levels respectively, and has consistently remained below the overall market level.  As a sustainable institution, the HKMA will continue to strive for progress, setting our sustainability goals and plans on the foundation of three pillars: environment, employees, and social responsibility. Specifically, in the HKMA's low-carbon transition journey, we continue to strengthen our capacity to address climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures encompass emissions reduction, energy efficiency improvements, and waste management, with the ultimate goal of fulfilling our commitment to achieving net zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have formulated plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the near term and have made solid progress toward our medium-term target of reducing Scope 2 emissions by 2030.  To attract and retain outstanding talent to fulfil the HKMA's important functions, in addition to our green goals, the HKMA is also committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of our staff. Furthermore, through collaboration with various stakeholders, we promote financial inclusion, enhance public financial literacy, and raise public awareness of financial fraud prevention, contributing to the building of a caring society.  The climate challenge is immense and acutely urgent. As economies around the world advance towards a more sustainable future, this journey is expected to bring profound changes to financing activities and asset allocation. This transformation carries significant risks, but will also be accompanied by unprecedented opportunities. As a leading global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in addressing these challenges. At the same time, we are well-positioned to seize the opportunities they present. The HKMA will fully support the industry in financing the low-carbon transition; continue to act as a responsible investor and sustainable institution, leading by example; and collaborate with like-minded partners to advance this critically important global agenda.  Eddie Yue Chief Executive

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are global in nature. The HKMA's sustainability objectives are to take a leadership role through its own policies and operations, to ensure that Hong Kong's financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to climate risk, and to support the transition to a more sustainable economy. Through active engagement with international and regional organisations, the HKMA will also contribute to the development of regional and global green and sustainable finance policies and standards. As the banking sector regulator, the HKMA will further strengthen the climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities of the banking sector. Specifically, the key priorities include: conducting a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices and holding a new round of consultation meetings as part of reviewing banks' progress in implementing supervisory requirements on climate risk management; continuing work on integrating climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; completing the second industry-wide climate risk stress-tested exercise and providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, as well as sharing observations and lessons learned with the industry; strengthening sustainability disclosures, including working with local authorities to align relevant requirements with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards as the global baseline, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's Pillar 3 framework for climate-related financial risks; and sharing guidance on transition planning best practices with the industry. To promote the healthy development of banks in offering green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to closely monitor local and international market and regulatory developments and maintain liaison with the industry to ensure that banks adopt appropriate sales processes. In addition, the HKMA will play the role of a facilitator in driving the development of the green finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the economic transition. We will soon launch the local green classification framework and continue to expand its coverage to include more activities such as transition activities. At the same time, we will continue to explore technology solutions to help banks identify, measure and monitor their climate risk exposures; one example is the forthcoming cloud-based platform to facilitate banks' physical risk assessment. To enhance practitioners' professional capabilities, we will also develop the "Green and Sustainable Finance" specialist module under the "Banking Professional Qualification Framework" in 2024. Hong Kong is well-positioned to serve as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfil this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the proposals in the 2023–24 Budget to expand the scope of the Government Green Bond Programme to cover sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bonds market; and attracting more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to be conducted in Hong Kong through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme. We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions and corporates to raise green funds in Hong Kong and explore potential synergies between green finance and technology. Furthermore, we will continue to assist in implementing the Government-funded Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme to expand Hong Kong's green finance talent pool. As co-chair of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies to coordinate cross-sector policies and initiatives to promote the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Steering Group will focus on three areas of work in 2024, including sustainable disclosures, application of technology, and transition finance. As another key focus, through the Green and Sustainable Finance Alliance, the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly launch various specialised programmes in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted professional training for banks, and providing practical guidance to support financial institutions in building their distinctive green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also deepen our collaboration with the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero, the Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance, and the Sustainable Finance Partnership for Green Development. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's portfolio by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of Exchange Fund investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring that the portfolio remains resilient on the path to net zero. Recognising that achieving an economy-wide transition is necessary to meet the goals of the Paris Agreement, we are refining our net-zero strategy to focus on assets that can generate positive climate outcomes for the real economy, while taking into account the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. As a green-conscious organisation, the HKMA's decarbonisation strategy will continue to evolve to reflect the latest developments in market, regulatory, technological, and other climate-related areas. To further strengthen the HKMA's climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technology solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. In addition, we will continue to actively encourage staff to participate in our sustainability efforts, including launching campaigns to cultivate sustainable habits and optimising office processes and practices. Furthermore, the HKMA will continue to maintain a consistent, efficient, and sustainable procurement approach, including assessing suppliers' ESG practices during contract selection and renewal. Building on the green data centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA is committed to upholding the designated certification standards. In relation to regular upgrades of data centre facilities, in addition to keeping pace with the latest technological developments, we will also incorporate green design and operational practices. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and convergence, and proactively modernise internal systems to improve efficiency and minimise potential risks. Finally, with regard to the social focus areas, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for colleagues, work with the industry to promote financial inclusion and enhance financial literacy, and raise public awareness of financial fraud prevention.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impact. The HKMA contributes to facilitating and accelerating the transition to net zero in Hong Kong and across Asia through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking sector regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable institution. The HKMA has in place a robust sustainability governance framework to lead the development of its sustainability strategies and policies, oversee the implementation of relevant measures, and ensure that sustainability factors are embedded in the HKMA's own operations and working practices. In pursuit of good institutional governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency for sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and that effective mechanisms are in place to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of sustainability work. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which are responsible for overseeing the HKMA's work, including its sustainability work, and providing recommendations; the Green and Sustainable Finance Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which leads the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategy and policies at the management level; in respect of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and in respect of other functional areas, relevant teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures ranging from banking and market development to the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the work of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's sustainability work over the past few years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA's different functional areas.¹ It provides guidance on the strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters across four functional areas, namely the banking sector, market development, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations; oversees the implementation of ESG-related initiatives by the HKMA's functional departments; assesses the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and oversees external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. In addition, the Executive Directors responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development matters will be invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on key outcomes and future plans for their respective work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Department, and Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to developing and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA co-initiated the Steering Group with the SFC in May 2020.² The Steering Group serves as a cross-agency platform to provide strategic direction and coordinate cross-sectoral work on the financial industry's response to climate and environmental risks, with a view to consolidating Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable financial centres in Asia and globally. Details of the Steering Group's work are set out in the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change is a significant risk to the financial system. The HKMA has been working to strengthen Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are affected by various sustainability and climate-related matters in their day-to-day business operations. To continue performing their vital functions in the financial system and to channel more funds towards green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risk. As the banking sector regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to respond to and manage climate risk, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The HKMA is committed to developing different policy measures to strengthen the banking system's resilience to climate risk.  In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to help banks maintain safety and soundness during the economy's transition to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of that circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey of certain banks in Q4 to understand their transition planning practices. Based on the survey findings, we will share observations and best practices on transition planning with the industry, and will organise seminars or workshops to facilitate experience-sharing among the industry.  On disclosure requirements, in response to the latest international developments — including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards published in June and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's (Basel Committee) consultation launched in November on a Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks — the HKMA is stepping up its efforts to enhance the sustainability-related disclosure framework for Hong Kong banks. Specifically, the HKMA is working with local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong aligned with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards.  During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and provided recommendations to banks to help them further enhance their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the bank supervisory process. Climate risk management has now been included as a standing agenda item in prudential meetings held with bank management. Bank examiners also adopted an enhanced CAMEL rating system1 that incorporates climate risk factors to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of the implementation of the two-year plan to embed climate risk factors into the bank supervisory process, the HKMA revised its "green" assessment framework to focus on banks' transition planning practices. The HKMA is also reviewing the Supervisory Review Process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with a view to encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks in addressing climate risk.  Key Focus Areas under the Two-Year Plan in 2023  Following the conclusion of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management", the HKMA conducted a round of thematic examinations on climate-related risk governance in Q2. The thematic examinations covered four areas: governance framework for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategy, oversight of climate-related risk management, and institutional culture, awareness and communication.  The HKMA made a number of enhancements to its climate risk stress-tested framework, including the introduction of a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of simultaneous economic and climate change shocks. Following these enhancements, and as part of the HKMA's regular regulator-led stress-testing programme, a second round of climate risk stress tests was launched in June to conduct a comprehensive assessment of banks' climate risk exposures and to further enhance banks' capacity to manage climate risk. A total of 44 banks participated in this round of stress tests, representing an increase of more than 60% compared to the first pilot exercise in 2021. The HKMA also organised a Climate Risk Stress Test Forum in November, which was attended by up to 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating experience-sharing among banks, the event helped deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk measurement.  The HKMA also conducted a series of supervisory meetings to review banks' progress in implementing Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management". The HKMA held meetings with bank management to discuss their work on climate risk management and common challenges faced by the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks as well as other publicly available information to assess their relevant progress. The HKMA provided targeted recommendations to banks to encourage and support them in continuing to enhance their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA's supervisory expectations.  As global attention and efforts to address climate change grow, the HKMA has noted increasing demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks offering such products to meet customer needs. In this regard, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks' sale of green and sustainable investment products, and issued a circular in November setting out the standards the HKMA expects banks to meet and sharing observed good practices. The circular covers areas including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training and record-keeping, with the aim of mitigating potential greenwashing risks and enhancing investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of such investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments.  The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analysis, enhancing banks' capacity to manage climate risk. The HKMA will soon launch a beta version of a cloud-based platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. In addition, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulators to explore how technology solutions can assist in physical risk assessments. On another front, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable approaches to anti-money laundering (AML) compliance through the application of advanced analytics and A.I., reducing the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online shared data submission platform to fully automate the financial crime risk data collection process, thereby enhancing banks' operational workflows for submitting AML-related data in a sustainable manner.  In September, the HKMA organised a "Green Fintech Competition" aimed at seeking market-ready solutions to help the banking sector address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosures and reporting. The competition attracted more than 85 entries from approximately 70 companies. In December, the HKMA organised a "Green and Sustainable Banking Seminar", providing a platform for the banking sector and the technology sector to explore the role of low-carbon technology and green fintech in Hong Kong's and the Mainland's net-zero transition, and the results of the "Green Fintech Competition" were announced at the same event. The event attracted approximately 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulators and academia.  To enhance transparency in financial markets and to bring greater consistency to green and sustainable finance decision-making, the HKMA, with the assistance of a consultancy firm, developed a local green classification framework. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on a "Prototype Hong Kong Green Taxonomy", seeking stakeholders' views on the establishment and implementation of a green taxonomy. Based on the consultation findings, the HKMA is fine-tuning the prototype framework and identifying additional areas for the next phase of framework development.  The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force, which has identified environmental crime as a predicate offence for money laundering, and this area is receiving increasing attention from more regulators in light of the interconnections between AML and environmental, social and governance (ESG) considerations.  Recognising the potential risks that climate change may pose to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risks analysis and research to strengthen current monitoring efforts. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and incorporates analysis of climate-related risks in various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the scenario design and analysis workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped to further enrich climate scenarios to give central banks and regulators a clearer understanding of the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. As a member of the Financial Stability Board's Workgroup on Transition Planning, the HKMA participates in the analysis of the interaction between transition planning by financial and non-financial firms and financial stability, enabling policymakers to take a forward-looking and dynamic view of climate-related financial risks.  On the research front, the HKMA conducted a number of applied research projects exploring the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial sector and the economy. Research topics included climate risk exposures in the banking sector and investment funds2, ESG fund flows3, the impact of climate change on housing prices4, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance in global supply chains5. The findings of these research projects enhance the HKMA's understanding of the impact of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability and contribute to the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, these research efforts help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risk on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA also shares research findings with a broad range of stakeholders through international engagements on climate-related matters and various channels such as HKMA Research Memoranda.  The HKMA's liquidity facilities framework is a secured backstop funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations in assessing eligible collateral under this framework in accordance with NGFS recommendations.  The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such engagement, the HKMA contributes to promoting international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its implications for financial stability, and draws insights from these discussions to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To reinforce Hong Kong's position as a leading regional green and sustainable finance hub, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and engagement, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to build a richer ecosystem and drive the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-led by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the Government's climate strategies. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key measures to support Hong Kong in capturing sustainable finance opportunities, with major areas of work covering sustainable disclosure, ecosystem building, transition finance, and green fintech. Specifically, a Sustainable Disclosure Workstream has been established to develop a roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The roadmap will cover four key areas, including sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. A Transition Finance Workstream was also established to explore ways to support financial institutions and enterprises in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group has also strengthened the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sectoral skills training and data enhancement. In particular regarding data, we continued to promote the adoption of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for unlisted companies, which was launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to keep abreast of the latest developments in green and sustainable finance and enhance Hong Kong's position as a regional and global green and sustainable finance hub. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key workstreams to capture investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia Pacific region. To support skills training in the industry, the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance under the Steering Group implemented the Government's Green and Sustainable Finance Talent Scheme, providing subsidies to practitioners, students, and graduates who undertake green and sustainable finance-related training and obtain relevant qualifications. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications had been registered as eligible training or qualifications under the scheme, with over 560 subsidy applications approved. The HKMA also launched the foundation level of a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for the banking sector. This module aims to foster talent development and enhance the overall professional competency of practitioners in the banking sector. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to work with the banking sector to develop the professional level of the module to meet the rapidly growing demand for green and sustainable finance professionals. To help financial institutions and enterprises, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, better understand key climate and sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation, and transition planning, the HKMA co-organised a series of seminars and thematic workshops during the year with relevant Government bureaux and departments as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. On student engagement, following the launch of the Sustainable Finance Internship Programme in 2022, training sessions were held in January and February 2023 to deepen interns' and undergraduate graduates' understanding of sustainable finance. Recognising the potential of technology in bridging climate-related data gaps and improving data quality, the HKMA is committed to making relevant data more accessible and improving data quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website enhancements to provide financial institutions, enterprises, and the public with a one-stop platform for green and sustainable finance information. Key enhancements include a sustainable disclosure e-platform, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, and more centralised, easily navigable, and searchable data and resources. During "Hong Kong Green Week", the Steering Group also co-organised the "Leveraging Technology for Sustainable Finance" event with Cyberport and Invest Hong Kong, showcasing leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's strengths in green technology. "Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Theme" was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, with various sustainability-themed events attracting over 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporations, central banks, international organisations, government agencies, academia, and consulting firms. The highlight event of "Hong Kong Green Week" was the Asia Pacific Climate Business Forum, co-organised by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation. The forum brought together over 400 guests, including leading decision-makers from the global business and financial sectors, to discuss ways to unlock climate finance in the Asia Pacific region. The two-day event covered a wide range of topics, including energy transition, decarbonisation of heavy industries, circular economy, the future of sustainable finance, and new climate technologies in emerging and developing markets in the Asia Pacific region. The forum garnered support from both the public and private sectors, co-hosting over 10 roundtables, seminars, and other exchange activities. Topics covered included climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chain, net-zero transition financing, green finance taxonomy, and green development financing in Belt and Road regions. In addition, the HKMA and the International Monetary Fund co-organised the "Asia Climate Finance Roundtable" on 29 February 2024 to discuss key measures to scale up climate finance and the role of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. These events form part of the HKMA's overall efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem and serve as useful platforms to help participants drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting regional green and sustainable finance development. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA launched the Green and Sustainable Banking Network as a collaborative platform bringing together regional financial institutions, banking associations, research institutions, and innovative technology providers to jointly advance green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the network has held 22 training events and roundtables, attracting over 7,300 participants from the Asia Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. In October, the network jointly published with Crédit Agricole CIB a second thought leadership report entitled "Developing Ambitious Climate Strategies for Green Banking: Case Studies". During the year, the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the newly established Capacity Building Alliance for Sustainable Investment (CASI) and the Green Investment and Financing Partnership (GIFP) initiated by the Belt and Road Green Development International Coalition. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, and channel more capital towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and beyond. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of its Hong Kong chapter to support the net-zero efforts of financial institutions in Hong Kong and Mainland China. The HKMA is assisting with GFANZ's work in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate the Government's commitment to addressing climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. The HKMA assists in the issuance of green bonds under the programme. To date, the Government has issued approximately US$25 billion equivalent of green institutional and Retail Bonds, with proceeds allocated to over 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the programme, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report detailing the allocation of proceeds from the green bonds and their expected environmental benefits. The Government continued its regular green institutional bond issuance programme in the 2023–24 fiscal year, issuing approximately US$6 billion equivalent of green bonds in June. The tri-currency issuance, covering US dollar, euro, and renminbi bonds of various tenors, attracted a diverse range of investors and was met with strong demand, recording nearly US$30 billion equivalent in subscriptions. The renminbi bond issuance was increased from RMB10 billion issued in January to RMB15 billion, with the addition of a 10-year renminbi bond for the first time, helping to extend the Government's renminbi yield curve and further enrich the CNH product offering. The strong response from global investors to the Government's green bond issuance reflects investors' recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued a second batch of green Retail Bonds with a total value of HKD20 billion to further promote market development and advance financial inclusion. This issuance provided members of the public with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, enabling them to participate in and benefit from Hong Kong's green finance development.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA plays a key role in promoting green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the HKMA has been leading the way in green and sustainable asset investment, requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership and integrating environmental, social and governance factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "preserving capital first, achieving long-term growth"1, and believes that giving due consideration to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps reduce relevant investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and set a "Net Zero by 2050" target2 for its portfolio, the HKMA is committed to continuously advancing its responsible investment journey, emphasising sustainability, particularly the urgent issue of climate change, with a view to enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and pursuing better risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA participates in building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem, working with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to develop industry operating standards, and promoting the adoption of responsible investment by the financial industry and central banks. Through stewardship and collaborative initiatives, the HKMA strives to foster a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. Figure 1: The Exchange Fund's Responsible Investment Journey Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is critical for integrating sustainability and planning a credible climate transition to achieve net-zero targets. In fulfilment of its commitment to support the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) Glasgow Declaration3 and the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group's strategic plan, the HKMA leads by example and prepares this chapter on the Exchange Fund's responsible investment in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The overarching guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to pursue the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund alongside responsible investment. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks in Exchange Fund investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management guidelines, and monitors implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing various ESG initiatives within the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Motions discussed and work progress at quarterly ESG Committee meetings are reported to the Chief Executive of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets semi-annually to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG objectives. Figure 2: Responsible Investment Governance Structure of the Exchange Fund Investment Office As shown in Figure 1, the Exchange Fund Investment Office commenced its responsible investment journey in 2016, with an initial focus on managing ESG risks that could affect the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainable development evolved rapidly and became a priority strategic focus for major institutions worldwide beyond risk considerations, the Exchange Fund Investment Office reviewed its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone when the Exchange Fund Investment Office established a new Business Strategy division led by the Chief Strategy Officer to coordinate and lead the Exchange Fund Investment Office's strategic development, incorporating the dedicated responsible investment team – now known as the Sustainable Investment team – previously under the Risk Management and Monitoring division. This strategic move reflects the HKMA's shift in responsible investment focus from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainability-related investment matters. The Sustainable Investment team works closely with different teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office on the integration of ESG factors and assists senior staff of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing ESG and, in particular, climate-related risks and opportunities across various investments: Public markets investments — The Credit, Regulatory and Monitoring Committee, comprising senior staff of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to the advice of the Sustainable Investment team, and monitors the ESG profile of fixed income portfolios through regular reports from the Risk Management and Monitoring division. In addition, the Sustainable Investment team participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios (see the "Promoting Active Ownership" section under "Risk Management" on page 40). Private markets investments — The Investment Committee chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA considers ESG-related assessments made by the private markets investment and risk management teams on each investment proposal. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks4 arising from climate change, as well as the related opportunities, will affect the long-term performance and value of Exchange Fund investments. The United Nations Environment Programme's Emissions Gap Report 20235 projects that global average temperatures will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030 unless further greenhouse gas emission reductions are made worldwide. The urgent need for more aggressive policies, technological development or behavioural change to keep temperature rise in check could intensify transition risks such as asset devaluation or stranded asset impacts. At the same time, extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and severe, posing additional physical risks to investments. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future is aligned with the Exchange Fund's investment objectives, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG factors. The HKMA's establishment in 2022 of a target for the Exchange Fund's portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier further demonstrates its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach with a clear focus on decarbonisation and transition. The relevant approaches are elaborated in the sections below. Figure 3: The HKMA's Three-Pronged Approach to Responsible Investment In its journey towards net-zero targets, the HKMA prefers active engagement over exclusion or divestment from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund's primary investment objectives. Direct exclusion of certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, with potential implications for investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess superior technology and sound corporate governance to navigate evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investments or divesting does not resolve the issue of carbon emissions. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries through the deployment of strategic capital and active exercise of asset ownership, encouraging them to transition to sustainable and low-carbon operational practices, thereby bringing about positive changes for themselves and the world. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net-zero investment strategies to pursue, through a comprehensive approach, transition outcomes aligned with the Exchange Fund's and global net-zero objectives, while adhering to its guiding principles of responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities to facilitate climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's asset portfolio (Figure 4). The HKMA's responsible investment maintained good momentum in 2023. On the public markets front, the HKMA launched a new active global equity portfolio themed around sustainability and climate transition, managed by an external investment manager, and expanded the application of customised low-carbon equity indices to another portfolio managed by an external investment manager. In addition, the green, social and sustainability bonds that the HKMA prioritised for investment outperformed the investment benchmark, demonstrating the concept of "doing good and doing well". On the private markets front, the HKMA actively built a resilient long-term growth portfolio, capturing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic development trends such as climate and energy transition. For example, during the year, the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds, reflecting the HKMA's commitment to addressing Asia's climate transition needs. Figure 4: Continued Implementation of Measures to Drive ESG Investment The HKMA has invested in a company that specialises in producing eco-friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted household waste (including organic materials such as food waste) and non-recyclable materials. Unlike conventional chemical recycling systems that rely on energy-intensive high-temperature environments for plastic production, this company has pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. This 100% waste-derived plastic material serves as a substitute for petroleum-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and consumer durables, providing a sustainable and versatile option. At the same time, this plastic material is compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies such as 3D printing. The company is firmly committed to the circular economy. The HKMA made two tranches of investment commitments of US dollar 1 billion each to MCPP in 2017 and 2019 respectively, and further collaborated with the International Finance Corporation to create the new global climate-related investment platform "MCPP One Planet" in 2021, which is also the world's first cross-sector emerging market loan portfolio aligned with the Paris Agreement. Through the MCPP programme, the HKMA has committed to providing loans to 80 sustainable development projects across 19 sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate and manufacturing, in 38 developing countries. The International Finance Corporation has collected data on MCPP loans. According to the International Finance Corporation's reports, the HKMA's loan commitments support emerging markets and developing countries in areas such as economic transition and human resources development. The HKMA is committed to being a sustainable organisation and adopts a multi-pronged approach to reducing its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also places great emphasis on employee wellbeing and social responsibility, and strives to advance financial inclusion and enhance the public's financial literacy. As a responsible organisation, the HKMA sets sustainability targets under three pillars: environment, people, and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee)¹, established in October and chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, serves as the principal decision-making body for the organisation's sustainability initiatives. The Steering Committee succeeded the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Committee, which was responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating the vision, strategy and policies for corporate sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Deputy Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and reports progress to the Steering Committee on a regular basis. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Services Team provide support for coordinating corporate sustainability efforts; the former serves as a platform for discussing ideas on creating a green working environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of volunteer participation. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transition pathway. Key efforts focus on implementing carbon reduction strategies in its day-to-day operations, including operating green buildings and data centres, practising green travel, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools and more environmentally friendly ways of working, reducing waste, and building a sustainability culture. The HKMA also plans to employ carbon-embedding tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and to apply carbon offset measures for emissions that are difficult to reduce. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to its daily operations, the HKMA continues to introduce greener operational solutions for the wider community, covering channels for banks to submit electronic documents and communications, as well as electronic payment and coin collection schemes for the general public. To strengthen and sustain its operational capacity, the HKMA employs a professional workforce, builds a talent pool, and places strong emphasis on employee wellbeing. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages staff to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers engaging social enterprises (SEs) in procurement; promotes financial services consumer education; and works with the banking sector to ensure equitable access to basic banking services for all members of society. The remainder of this chapter sets out the details of these strategies. Under the HKMA's overall corporate risk management framework, the Risk Committee², chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the potential risks and threats facing the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as increased extreme weather events causing flooding or other damage, could affect the HKMA's offices and impede staff movement.
