To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plans to address extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure staff are always prepared to implement business continuity measures. The design of the offices also incorporates various measures to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA's energy use, air travel, and waste disposal. The HKMA monitors its transition risks by tracking its own greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, waste generation, and energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's climate target is to achieve net-zero GHG emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel) in all areas of its operations by 2050 or earlier. As near-term emission reduction targets, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all of its existing vehicles to electric vehicles, and to reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier against a 2015 baseline through various carbon reduction and offset strategies. Despite the challenges in quantifying Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will adopt a multi-pronged approach to the extent practicable to minimise Scope 3 GHG emissions (e.g. from paper consumption, waste generation and air travel). The HKMA's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets were developed with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) methodology, which has been verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA). The HKMA has appointed the HKQAA to verify its disclosed emissions, energy and paper consumption data, and waste data as disclosed in this report⁶. The scope and basis of verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the 2022 Annual Report, the HKMA published its 2022 Sustainability Report as a standalone document for the first time. The HKMA's enhanced ESG reporting was recognised when it received the ESG Award in the "Public Sector Category" at the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023". The HKMA was the first financial regulatory authority to receive an award in this category. The judging panel commended the HKMA for meeting good ESG standards, for its clear and readable Sustainability Report, and for engaging an independent party to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report, reflecting its commitment to reporting with a high degree of transparency and accountability. In addition, the HKMA received the highest rating of gold award in the "Non-profit Making and Charitable Organisations" category at the Hong Kong Management Association's "Best Annual Reports Awards 2023". The judging panel commended the HKMA's annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and making good use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA's commitment to enhancing financial literacy and promoting financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, its employees, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has presented the HKMA with the "15 Years+" Caring Organisation Logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impact of its operations. Its internal Green Office Guidelines provide staff with guidance on resource use and the generation of office waste. The HKMA has incorporated environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. During office renovation works, existing furniture and fitting-out materials are reused wherever possible to reduce waste, and environmentally friendly building and decorative materials are given priority. The HKMA has consistently adopted this approach, and as a result, received Gold certifications under LEED⁷ and "BEAM Plus Interiors"⁸ in 2021 and 2022 respectively for the renovated portions of its offices at Two International Finance Centre. Adopting new technologies and making better use of existing technologies to improve energy efficiency remain among the HKMA's key priorities. In addition to promoting good habits, such as switching off unnecessary lighting in work areas outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include the use of LED lighting equipment, occupancy sensors, setting air conditioning temperatures at appropriate levels, and optimising energy use in IT network infrastructure. The HKMA's energy consumption has continued to decrease, reaching 2.59 megawatt-hours per capita⁹ in 2023, a reduction of 29.7% from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA's day-to-day operations, its GHG emissions are primarily attributable to GHG emissions generated from the consumption of electricity produced from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO₂e¹⁰ per capita, a reduction of 45.2% from 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardising equipment, office software and conferencing facilities, the HKMA has adopted digital tools and technologies, and automated and streamlined workflows to build a digital working environment and strengthen online collaboration within the organisation.¹¹ Paperless meetings have become the primary mode of conducting meetings at the HKMA. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, electronic processes are used primarily for various internal administrative matters. In addition, the HKMA encourages staff to embrace green and digital working practices by replacing paper-based documents and communications with digital alternatives. At the same time, work is in progress to implement an electronic records management system. These green and digital measures have yielded positive results. The HKMA's paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kilograms per capita, a significant reduction of 64.8% from 2015 (Figure 3). Following the resumption of most international events in physical format after the COVID-19 pandemic, and given the need to promote Hong Kong's status as an international financial centres, it is inevitable that relevant HKMA staff are required to travel overseas on business. To reduce the carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to take direct flights or consolidate different business trips where practicable when participating in overseas events. At the corporate level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO₂e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. In addition, the HKMA participates in a "Gold Standard"¹²-certified carbon offset programme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; the programme involves waste-to-energy, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue with similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA's procurement processes take sustainability and environmental factors into account. As part of a comprehensive review of the organisation's procurement policies and procedures, the current practice of procuring green products has been formalised as an established system, adhering to the environmental specifications set out in the government's "Green Procurement List", particularly in the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. Furthermore, ESG factors and innovative proposals that help enhance productivity and efficiency have been incorporated into tender evaluation criteria. All suppliers are also required to commit to compliance with environmental regulations. Following the "4R" principles — Refuse, Reduce, Reuse and Recycle — the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimise waste generation and manage waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to assist in formulating targeted waste management strategies. Details of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, are set out in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA participated for the first time directly in the red packet recycling scheme organised by the building management company of its offices at the International Finance Centre. Staff collectively submitted approximately 3,000 used but still pristine red packets. These red packets were subsequently passed to an environmental organisation for distribution to the public for use during the upcoming Lunar New Year. Given that the HKMA's operational and backup data centres account for a significant portion of the organisation's overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centres, achieving optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE)¹³. In 2023, the HKMA's two data centres received "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings respectively under "BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres", assessed in accordance with assessment guidelines issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only organisation in Hong Kong to have received such ratings. Improving the energy efficiency of the two data centres has long been a key priority for the technology team. To this end, the team has adopted green design in renovation works and implemented energy-efficient best practices to reduce PUE and achieve the relevant targets, including 24-hour monitoring of the environmental facilities of the data centres and continuous improvement of environmental factors such as airflow and temperature settings. As the technology team continued to improve energy use in the data centres, the HKMA engaged an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review to comprehensively assess the green performance of the data centres and formulate recommendations to further enhance performance across various areas. The study was completed in mid-2022. The HKMA also began preparing for BEAM Plus certification under the "Green Data Centre" certification programme shortly after the completion of the study. The certification process is comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the technology team implemented optimisation measures in accordance with the recommendations of the consultant's report, improving energy performance as well as health elements of the working environment within the data centres.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's ("HKMA") 2023 Environmental Data ("2023 Data"). The 2023 Data includes the total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, business air travel greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), their respective intensities, and the changes in the data compared to the 2015 baseline. In addition, the 2023 Data also includes the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared to the level when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data has been compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, as well as the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison (except for food waste). The verification scope covers a total of 5 office and warehouse asset, of which 4 offices are located at 1) Two International financial centres, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Pacific Place One, 4) Landmark East, and a warehouse at 5) Lacsonic Industrial Centre, located in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 5 asset. This verification was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to express an opinion and conclusions to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was defined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to its source, and reviewed and tested the reliability of the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and selecting representative data and information for review. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also subject to detailed examination during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work is entirely independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the preparation of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 Data and concludes that: the 2023 Data is materially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA's overall data collection mechanisms are adequate. Shen Xiaoyin, Review Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, April 2024

The threat of climate change is imminent, making it increasingly urgent to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record and the first year in which global temperatures exceeded the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, global greenhouse gas emissions, which moderated briefly during COVID-19, have recently reached new highs, underscoring the inadequacy of current climate mitigation measures. As the world grapples with global warming, climate-related risks will inevitably intensify, with unpredictable consequences for economies and financial markets. Compounding this are heightened geopolitical tensions, increasing fragmentation of the global economic landscape, growing energy security concerns, and an uncertain economic outlook — all of which pose greater challenges for countries in addressing climate change.  The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. This challenge is particularly acute in Asia. As the World Economic Forum has noted, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Asia therefore plays a pivotal role in determining whether the world can successfully achieve net-zero emissions. As Asia's leading international financial centres, Hong Kong must strengthen its leadership role and harness the power of finance to support and drive the region's transition. To this end, the HKMA published its Sustainable Finance Action Plan last year, setting out our vision and roadmap for progressively embedding sustainability into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on both enhancing the financial industry's capacity to manage climate-related risks and helping the industry seize the new opportunities that arise. We also lead by example.  The HKMA's sustainability work encompasses four key areas: supporting the banking sector's journey to net zero, investing in a sustainable future, facilitating net-zero financing, and promoting more inclusive sustainable development.  The banking system plays a critical role in Hong Kong's and Asia's net-zero transition, but banks themselves face considerable risks in the process. In the Action Plan, we set ambitious targets requiring all banks to commit to achieving net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero in their financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. We also require all banks to strengthen their disclosure of climate-related risks and opportunities. Alongside our ongoing efforts to enhance banks' climate risk management, we are providing guidance on transition planning to help banks build their transition capabilities and better manage associated risks. We are also working with relevant stakeholders on preparatory measures to align Hong Kong's sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, with a view to further improving transparency across the industry in this area. In addition, we are refining the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance, launched in May last year, to incorporate more sustainable activities, including transition activities. We hope that by providing clear criteria, we can direct greater flows of capital towards sustainable and transition-related projects.  Climate change gives rise to significant physical and transition risks that may affect the long-term financial performance and value of Exchange Fund investments. At the same time, it also presents opportunities for the Exchange Fund to achieve growth and generate positive impact. Our experience has shown that investment returns and positive sustainable impact are complementary — there is no inherent conflict between the two. With this in mind, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's portfolio by 2050 or earlier, and in the Action Plan we have pledged to support Asia's climate transition through Exchange Fund investments. Sustainable investments currently account for more than 10% of the portfolio. To further advance sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships in November last year with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation, co-investing to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in Asia. We also published our inaugural HKMA ESG Expectations document in September last year to further encourage fund managers to actively exercise asset ownership rights and adopt sound sustainable investment practices.  Financing is of particular importance in accelerating the regional transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for Asian issuers — including Mainland provincial and municipal governments — to arrange international sustainable bond issuances, Hong Kong plays an important role in channelling capital to accelerate the regional transition. The Action Plan sets out our vision of developing Hong Kong into the region's preferred sustainable finance platform, and our goal of fostering sustainable finance innovation. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the Government Green Bond Programme to drive green bond innovation — including the issuance of the world's first multi-currency digital bonds in February last year — to expanding the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme to cover transition financing instruments in May last year, and the launch of the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November last year, we have been consistently encouraging regional issuers to use Hong Kong's financial platform to raise capital for their decarbonisation transitions.  A robust transition requires not only capital and innovation, but also an inclusive and accessible sustainable development ecosystem. This includes reliable sustainability data, highly transparent disclosure, and industry talent equipped with the relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, the Action Plan commits us to supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure, and to bridging the sustainable finance talent and knowledge gap in the region. We have made good progress in assisting stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosure — in particular by providing user-friendly climate disclosure templates to support small and medium-sized enterprises in their sustainability reporting. We also launched the Green and Sustainable Finance professional-level module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for banking practitioners in November last year, to strengthen the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking professionals. Furthermore, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we have engaged stakeholders from across sectors in discussions on sustainable development, fostering collaboration and innovation.  Within the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations reflect our sustainability vision. We have pledged in the Action Plan to achieve net-zero in our own operations by 2030 or earlier — 20 years ahead of our original commitment. We are also actively preparing to meet international sustainable disclosure standards in accordance with the government's published roadmap. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and have incorporated low-carbon emissions as a screening criterion in our procurement process. We continue to enhance operational efficiency through digitalisation, fostering a culture of sustainability within the organisation and encouraging staff to actively participate in sustainability initiatives.  Multilateral cooperation has long been the cornerstone of global efforts to address climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and dramatic shifts in geopolitical dynamics have introduced new uncertainties into global climate action. Nevertheless, climate change is an undeniable reality that is intensifying. In addressing it, there is no room for complacency. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help reduce the impact of climate risk on Hong Kong's financial system and create opportunities along the way. As we enter 2025, we will continue to press forward with our sustainability work and deepen our relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the formidable challenges ahead, we remain steadfast in our commitment to supporting Hong Kong, Asia, and beyond in building a sustainable future.

Climate change is one of the most significant challenges facing our generation. As an international financial centres and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development across Asia and beyond. In October 2024, the HKMA published its Sustainable Finance Action Plan (the "Action Plan"), setting out the HKMA's vision in this area, including our future directions, a timeline for achieving various goals, and how we expect the industry to work together in advancing the relevant initiatives. The HKMA plans to strengthen the financial sector's and its own capacity to manage climate risk, and to drive Asia's transition to a more sustainable economy, through formulating strategic policies, enhancing regulatory connections, and improving internal operations. Through active participation in international and regional discussions, the HKMA also strives to exercise influence in shaping green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels. As a banking sector regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector and supporting banks in remaining safe and sound as they transition to net-zero emissions. Our priorities in 2025 include: - Conducting a new thematic review on banks' climate risk management practices, and holding a third round of consultation meetings to assess banks' implementation of the HKMA's relevant supervisory requirements and to further strengthen banks' climate risk management capabilities; - Finalising the work to incorporate climate risk stress-tested into the HKMA's regulator-led stress testing framework; - Continuing to advance the integration of climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; - Commencing preparatory work for developing supervisory requirements for the local banking sector to implement the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's forthcoming Pillar 3 disclosure framework on climate-related financial risks and the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards); - Completing the drafting of new module GS-2 of the Supervisory Policy Manual to provide guidance to banks on transition planning; and - Sharing with the industry good practices on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. Beyond its role as a banking sector regulator, the HKMA also serves as a facilitator, committed to promoting the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the transition. We have published Phase 1 of the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance, providing the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitate the flow of relevant funds. The HKMA has commenced Phase 2 of the taxonomy to expand its coverage, including the addition of transition elements, more green economic activities, and climate adaptation objectives. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will host another green fintech event in 2025 to encourage banks to adopt green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well-positioned to support the region's sustainable financing needs. To consolidate this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the Government Green and Sustainable Bond Programme, which has been expanded to cover sustainable projects, such as social projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bonds market and serve as a reference for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide subsidies through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platform to raise sustainable funds. We will also step up our promotional efforts to encourage more Mainland and overseas governments, institutions, and corporates to raise green capital in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing subsidies to prospective digital green bond issuers through the Digital Bond Grant Scheme. While the demand for high-quality sustainable disclosures from institutions and corporates continues to grow, the capacity and readiness of different entities to make such disclosures vary, and some may require additional guidance and support. In light of this, the HKMA will continue to work with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainable disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with richer climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainable disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how technology can be leveraged to make existing resources more accessible; and collaborate with major local industry associations to provide the training that the industry needs. The sustainable finance financial markets are rapidly evolving, necessitating an expansion of the local talent pool and the bridging of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and across the region. The HKMA's key initiatives in 2025 include working with the banking sector to develop the professional-level training curriculum for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Banking Professional Qualification Framework", and identifying areas where the industry requires further training through the upcoming Future Banking Talent 2026–2030 study. In addition, we plan to work with key stakeholders to enhance the promotion of the Government-funded Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme and review its scope of application. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the Green Commercial Banking Alliance to launch targeted initiatives in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market insights, offering targeted upskilling and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to help banks develop roadmaps to make green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA has committed the Exchange Fund's portfolio to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier in support of the broader economic transition. We will continuously enhance the sustainability of Exchange Fund investments through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, with a primary focus on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can generate positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to setting an example in institutional sustainability. In response to the accelerated net-zero commitment timeline announced in the Action Plan, the HKMA will progressively integrate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting at a pragmatic pace to continue driving institutional sustainability. Specifically, in 2025 we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring we focus on matters of significance. We will also conduct an energy audit and use technology solutions to assess the material impact of climate risk on our offices and operations, in order to enhance our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Government's publication of the Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap and are actively making preparations to make disclosures in accordance with ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to selecting data centres for planned upgrade projects in accordance with energy efficiency and conservation principles. We will also expand our digital initiatives to promote sustainability and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and improving the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the general public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impact. The HKMA, through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking sector regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable institution, contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has a robust sustainability governance framework to lead the formulation of its sustainability-related strategies and policies, oversee the implementation of relevant measures, and ensure that sustainability factors are embedded in the HKMA's own operations and working practices. In its commitment to sound institutional governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency for sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and that effective mechanisms are in place to monitor and evaluate the progress and effectiveness of sustainability efforts. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: - The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its dedicated sub-committees, which oversee the work of the HKMA, including its sustainability-related work, and make recommendations; - The Green and Sustainable Finance Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, which leads the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; - On responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and - For other functional areas, relevant teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures spanning banking sector and market development through to the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the work of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's sustainability work over recent years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA's different functional areas. The Steering Committee's responsibilities include: - Providing guidance on the formulation of ESG-related strategies, policies, and plans across four functional areas: the banking sector, development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations; - Overseeing the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's functional departments; - Evaluating the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and - Overseeing external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, with three Deputy Chief Executives as standing members. We also invite the relevant Executive Directors responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on key outcomes and future plans for their respective work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, Corporate Services and Operations Department, External Department, and Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA and the SFC co-initiated the establishment of the Steering Group in May 2020. The Steering Group serves as a cross-agency platform to provide strategic direction and coordinate cross-sectoral work on managing climate and environmental risks in the financial industry, with a view to consolidating Hong Kong's position among the leading green and sustainable financial centres in Asia and globally. For further details on the work of the Steering Group, please refer to the chapter on "Advancing the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been working to strengthen the Hong Kong financial system's resilience to climate risk, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are exposed to a wide range of sustainability and climate-related issues in their day-to-day operations, and must therefore proactively manage climate risk. At the same time, banks play a crucial role in the financial system in channelling funds towards green and sustainable projects. As the banking sector regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to address and manage climate risk, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA published its Sustainable Finance Action Plan (Action Plan), setting out the HKMA's vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainable financial centres hub and to support sustainable development across Asia and globally. The Action Plan comprises eight goals across four areas. To assist the industry in achieving the objectives of the relevant banking policies, we have been carrying out the following work. All banks to achieve net-zero operational emissions by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. All banks to increase transparency on climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices on transition planning with the industry and launched an industry consultation on a draft of Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) module GS-2 "Transition Planning". The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capacity to address net-zero transition and related risk management. In addition, we are reviewing the Supervisory Review Process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating relevant factors identified by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) for the effective management of climate-related financial risks, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks (including transition planning) to address climate risk. The HKMA has been working to align local sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, including the ISSB Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) and the Basel Committee's Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainable disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is central to implementing the Action Plan. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (Taxonomy) to address industry concerns about greenwashing and to help channel funds towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors, and is designed to align with the Common Ground Taxonomy as well as the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while incorporating elements that reflect local circumstances. We have commenced Phase 2 work to expand the scope of the Taxonomy and are consulting a broad range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable capital. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and worked to support banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and to respond to climate change. The HKMA also completed all work under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to incorporate climate risk into banking supervisory processes. To promote banks' capacity in managing climate risk, the HKMA shared with the banking sector good practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation meetings, covering key areas including: - Establishing robust governance frameworks with clearly defined responsibilities for the Board and senior management - Ensuring effective oversight of key areas of climate-related risk issues: (1) facilitating and overseeing the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a sound climate risk culture within the institution. The HKMA held a Balanced Regulation roundtable in August focused on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on a range of climate risk-related topics, including challenges faced by banks in climate risk management, climate risk stress-tested exercises, transition planning, and finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and contributed to the HKMA's work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA conducted a round of thematic reviews of banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, and assessed their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in SPM module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management". The thematic reviews covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA held a second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new cohort of banks in implementing SPM module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" and to understand the challenges they faced. The consultation meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing. We provided feedback and guidance tailored to individual banks' circumstances to support their climate risk management efforts. The HKMA completed the second round of the Banking Sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) in 2024, with the participation of 21 retail banks and Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups. The results showed that, under various scenarios — including those assuming the simultaneous occurrence of climate risk and macroeconomic downturns — the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot exercise, participating banks significantly enhanced their capacity to measure and assess climate risk. A report setting out the CRST results and good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. Fully aware of the potential risks that climate change may pose to the financial system, the HKMA has been pursuing a number of initiatives to promote the use of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the HKMA launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risk on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform by incorporating user feedback and additional local data. In addition, the HKMA collaborated with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services industry. During the year, we published practical application guides and two Regtech Use Case Briefs (in English) on technology solutions for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also organised the third edition of "FiNETech", bringing together more than 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore green fintech collaboration. Recognising the potential risks that climate change may pose to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing monitoring work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its continuous monitoring of financial stability risks, and incorporates analysis of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the scenario design and analysis working groups under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped to further enrich climate scenarios, which assist central banks and regulators in understanding the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS published the fifth vintage of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Financial Stability Board's Transition Planning Working Group, the HKMA participates in analysing the interaction between transition planning by financial and non-financial firms and financial stability, enabling policymakers to assess climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published a "Practical Guide for Banks on the Application of Green Technology" (in English), providing financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. On the research front, the HKMA conducted a number of applied research projects exploring the impact of climate change on the financial industry and the broader economy. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of firms' environmental performance in their resilience to monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial industry in the transition to a low-carbon economy. The findings of this research not only deepened our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability, but also provided valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem to inform policy formulation. At the local level, this research helps strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The findings are also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through international forums and various channels, including HKMA Research Memoranda. The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (HKIMR), the research arm of the Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The research provided evidence that low-emission firms can derive significant benefits from carbon pricing, and highlighted its role in improving efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The research was published in the HKIMR's Insights from Monetary Research and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers. The HKMA's liquidity facilities framework is a collateralised contingent funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such engagement, we help facilitate international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its implications for financial stability, and draw on lessons learned to help strengthen the Hong Kong financial system's climate resilience.

To reinforce Hong Kong's position as a leading regional green and sustainable finance hub, the HKMA is committed to raising market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA's Sustainable Finance Action Agenda, the HKMA is dedicated to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to positioning Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform for regional and global borrowers, supporting technology innovation in green areas of the financial markets, enhancing sustainable disclosure in the industry, expanding the local pool of green talent, and addressing knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region.  Positioning Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform for the region and globally Catalysing sustainable finance innovation Supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure Addressing talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region  To demonstrate the Government's commitment to tackling climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing approximately US$28 billion equivalent of green bonds to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds have been allocated to more than 110 government green projects, covering areas such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and conservation, among others. We have leveraged each issuance opportunity to continually innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors and distribution channels, thereby laying the groundwork for other public and private sector green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the Programme's impact and further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the scope of the Programme was expanded to cover sustainable projects, and it was renamed the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" (Sustainable Bond Programme).  To enhance transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report, detailing the allocation of proceeds from the green bonds and their expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing approximately US$3 billion equivalent of institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This tri-currency issuance comprised bonds in renminbi, US dollar and euro across various tenors. The bonds attracted strong participation from a diverse range of investors, with total subscriptions of more than US$15 billion equivalent. The 20-year and 30-year renminbi green bonds were the Government's first ever such issuances and represent the longest-tenor renminbi bonds issued by the Government to date, providing new benchmarks for the market and further demonstrating the exemplary role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enriched the investment options available in Hong Kong's offshore renminbi (CNH) market. In addition, the enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government's green bond issuances reflects their recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development.  To encourage more regional borrowers to utilise Hong Kong's financing platform to raise funds for sustainable development, the HKMA continued to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, launched in May 2021, which provides subsidies for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The Scheme has been well received by the industry. As at end-2024, the Scheme had approved grants for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value of over US$140 billion. The Scheme was extended by three years to 2027 in May 2024 and expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the Scheme is to encourage borrowers in relevant sectors in the region to utilise Hong Kong's transition financing platform to progressively reduce carbon emissions.  - Approved grants for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value of over US$140 billion (as at end-2024) - Extended by three years to 2027 and expanded to cover transition financing instruments  Meanwhile, the HKMA's active promotion of Hong Kong's sustainable financing platform has yielded positive results. In August, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time, totalling RMB7 billion, comprising RMB2.7 billion green bonds, RMB1 billion sustainable bonds and RMB0.9 billion social bonds. In September, the People's Government of Guangdong Province issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, totalling RMB5 billion, including RMB1.5 billion green bonds. In October, the People's Government of Hainan Province also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, totalling RMB3 billion, including RMB1 billion blue bonds and RMB1 billion sustainable bonds. These bond issuance activities have repeatedly highlighted Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating green and sustainable fund flows between the Mainland and the rest of the world. Through these measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as Asia's preferred sustainable financing platform. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong continued to be the largest hub in Asia for arranging the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds in 2024, with a total of US$43.1 billion of such bonds arranged through Hong Kong, representing 45% of the regional total.  To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark tokenised green bond issuances in 2023 and 2024 — the world's first tokenised government green bonds and the world's first multi-currency digital bonds respectively. These issuances demonstrate the Government's support for market participants in the region to apply asset tokenisation and innovative technology in the field of green and sustainable finance. In November, the HKMA also launched the Digital Bond Grant Scheme to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovation in Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance market.  The Working Group on Sustainable Disclosure under the Cross-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (Steering Group) has been working towards the adoption of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards in Hong Kong. In December 2024, the Government published the Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap, providing a clear pathway for large public interest entities to fully adopt the ISSB standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to support entities at different stages of readiness in achieving high-quality sustainable disclosure, making sustainable disclosure more accessible and inclusive.  Notably, we continue to encourage the use of the "Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Unlisted Companies" (Questionnaire), developed by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainable disclosure by companies, including small and medium-sized enterprises. An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024, enabling companies to complete it online (see QR code below). The HKMA is refining the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly, including identifying the core questions in the Questionnaire and providing common use-case scenarios. In addition, we are working to enhance the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools on the Steering Group's website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage.  The HKMA leads by example by making high-quality sustainable disclosures in its Sustainability Report in accordance with the latest global standards, demonstrating its commitment. The Report contains rich content on the HKMA's climate-related institutional operational risks, as well as plans and progress towards achieving its climate targets. For details of our sustainable disclosures relating to our own operations, please refer to the chapter "A Sustainable HKMA".  Given the rapidly evolving sustainable finance market, the HKMA is stepping up skills training in the banking sector and facilitating knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders to address knowledge and talent gaps. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners in sustainable finance, the HKMA and the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB) jointly launched the Foundation Level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for the banking sector in July 2023. The module is designed to help banking professionals acquire knowledge and develop professional competencies in green and sustainable finance more effectively, and covers four key job functions: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainable/climate risk management; (3) sustainable disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainable strategy, compliance and controls. In addition, the Professional Level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, targeting mid- to senior-level banking practitioners responsible for relevant work, was launched in November.  To provide the necessary training for banking practitioners, the HKIB, as the administrator of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, launched the Foundation Level training courses for the module in May. Following the launch of the Professional Level in November, the HKMA will work with the banking sector in 2025 to develop training courses for the Professional Level. To better understand the further skills and training needs of the banking sector, the HKMA is currently collaborating with the banking sector to conduct the "Future of Banking Talent 2026–2030" study, with the aim of publishing the findings in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the "Future of Banking Talent 2021–2025" document published in June 2020. The findings of the follow-up study will provide important reference for the industry in formulating and adjusting talent training strategies and initiatives to support the sustainable development of the banking sector.  The HKMA also continues to assist in implementing the Government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" through collaboration with the Steering Group, which subsidises practitioners, graduates and students for sustainable finance-related training. As at December 2024, the Scheme had 85 international and local courses registered as eligible training courses and had approved over 5,700 reimbursement applications. The Government announced in the Budget for 2025–26 that the Scheme will be extended to 2028.  The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience through regional and international collaboration to promote skills training and knowledge sharing. As a founding member of the Capacity Building Alliance for Sustainable Investment (CASI), the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-organised a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussions centred on global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks and innovative instruments. In addition, the HKMA supported the establishment of a chapter of the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can go hand in hand, the HKMA adheres to the principles of responsible investment in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritising sustainable assets and requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership. Guided by the principle of "preserving capital first, long-term appreciation", the HKMA invests prudently, believing that due consideration of environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment work. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieving better risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continually exploring various investment instruments to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to advancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made the document available to investment partners through annual ESG workshops and the HKMA website. We work with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to co-develop industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial industry and central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we strive to foster a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA announced its "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), which sets out its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions across the Exchange Fund portfolio by 2050 or earlier and mobilising partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, further solidifying its commitment to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee (EFAC), chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The overarching guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to pursue responsible investment while balancing the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the EFAC, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks in Exchange Fund investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management guidelines, and monitors implementation through regular reports from the EFIO's Sustainable Investment team. As illustrated in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG work across the EFIO. Initiatives and work progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the EFIO. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the EFIO, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the EFIO, in pursuit of the HKMA's overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment team works closely with different teams within the EFIO on ESG integration and assists senior EFIO staff in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across investment portfolios:  - Public Market Investments – The Credit, Compliance and Review Committee, comprising senior EFIO staff, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to input from the Sustainable Investment team, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Monitoring Division. In addition, the Sustainable Investment team participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios (see the "Promoting Active Ownership" section under "Risk Management" on page 39 for details).  - Private Market Investments – The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal.  The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks of climate change, as well as related opportunities, will affect the long-term financial performance of Exchange Fund investments. The United Nations Environment Programme's "Emissions Gap Report 2024" projects that global average temperatures will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels unless rapid, large-scale mobilisation to reduce greenhouse gas emissions is undertaken globally. Uncertainties in policy changes, technological developments and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may heighten transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and impacting asset valuation. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also pose additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investments. Amid these challenges, the shift by governments and industries towards sustainable solutions also creates investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies and sustainable infrastructure that may offer attractive long-term prospects. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future is aligned with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG factors. The HKMA has set a target of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund portfolio by 2050 or earlier, and is continuously advancing its work through an orderly three-pronged approach to achieve this goal (see Figure 3). The HKMA published the "Action Plan" in 2024, which consolidates the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA favours active engagement over exclusion or divestment from investable assets.  Investing in a Sustainable Future – Exchange Fund Portfolio to Achieve Net-Zero Emissions by 2050 or Earlier  - Actively expand the scope and types of sustainable investments, particularly climate transition-themed investments in public and private markets - Integrate ESG factors in every investment decision, with particular focus on climate change and transition pathway considerations - Establish clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, and require all external investment managers, investee companies and counterparties to comply - Target a 67% reduction in the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio from 2017 levels by 2030 or earlier  Supporting Regional Transition Through Investments  - Continue to engage with external investment managers to optimise investment opportunities that drive transition - Continue to identify and prioritise quality investment opportunities that promote Asia's transition and deliver positive global impact  First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the Exchange Fund's primary investment objectives. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risk. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA is able to seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition and possessing advanced technology and strong corporate governance to navigate evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emission industries.  Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding or divesting from such investments does not address carbon emissions. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries through deploying strategic capital and active ownership to drive their transition to sustainable and low-carbon operating practices, thereby bringing about positive change for themselves and for the world at large. Net-zero investment approaches have evolved from favouring green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition pathways, in order to drive economy-wide decarbonisation.  As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of the portfolio depends not only on portfolio-level adjustments, but also on broader economic transition. While there is no single perfect solution, the HKMA refined its responsible investment strategies in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting the Exchange Fund's and global net-zero objectives. The strategies combine top-down and bottom-up tools, including integrating ESG factors and stewardship into fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilts, and thematic investments targeting assets aligned with net-zero pathways. In public markets, this may involve tilting the portfolio towards ESG leaders or climate solution providers, complemented by stewardship to drive corporate transition. In private markets, the focus may be more on transition-enabling investments. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continuously identifies investment opportunities that can promote climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's portfolio.  Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund portfolio, with financial performance comparable to the relevant portfolio benchmarks (Figure 5).  - Public Market Investments – The HKMA launched an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the application of customised low-carbon equity indices to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek green, social and sustainability (GSS) bonds that provide competitive returns while funding sustainable projects (see the "Enhancing Sustainability Through GSS Bonds" section for related case studies).  - Private Market Investments – The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio by capturing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA actively identifies and assesses investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including through establishing strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (see the "Collaborating to Address Climate Challenges in Asia and Beyond" section for examples).  - Passive portfolios benchmarked against ESG indices - Customised decarbonisation strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios benchmarked against non-ESG indices - Active portfolios with a governance theme - Active ESG portfolios themed on sustainability and climate transition - Projects with sustainable characteristics, such as renewable energy infrastructure, and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed on energy transition and decarbonisation in global, Asian and Global South markets - Green, social and sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The "Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Programme" (MCPP) managed by the International Finance Corporation, focused on sustainable projects in emerging markets - "MCPP One Planet", providing climate-related investments in emerging markets aligned with the Paris Agreement  The HKMA invested in green bonds issued by a quasi-government institution. The proceeds from the green bonds were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading ageing equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrades encompassed optimising monitoring and control systems and pump performance to generate environmental benefits through wastewater management, waste reduction and recycling. In addition to the ongoing treatment of wastewater and sludge, these facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertilisers, charcoal, cement and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recovery rate of up to 100%. The facilities also utilise gases generated during the sludge treatment process to power boilers and generate electricity.  The HKMA invested in green bonds issued by a multilateral development bank. The bonds financed multiple projects, including the rehabilitation of a national canal system. As one of the country's largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess water from rivers to arid areas. The primary purpose of the project is to rehabilitate deteriorating canal linings to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water use efficiency and reclaim waterlogged areas. In addition, the project provides skills training for local stakeholders to promote the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation techniques such as micro-irrigation and sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organisation. One of the HKMA's key areas of work in 2024 in delivering on this commitment was the plan to bring forward the target for achieving net-zero emissions from its institutional operations to 2030, which is 20 years ahead of the original target, in line with the Sustainable Finance Action Agenda. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is also committed to fostering staff training and well-being, and to advancing financial inclusion and enhancing the public's financial literacy. The Green and Sustainable Finance Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, serves as the primary decision-making body for institutional sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 the HKMA's new target of achieving net-zero emissions from its institutional operations by 2030 or before, as part of the Sustainable Finance Action Agenda (Action Agenda). At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Institutional Development and Operations) provides guidance on implementing sustainability measures relating to institutional operations, staff well-being and community engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Corporate Services Department serves as the coordinator and central hub for implementing, communicating and reporting institutional sustainability measures. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Team, both comprising staff from different operational departments, provide an additional layer of support; the former is a platform for brainstorming and making recommendations on how to create a greener work environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of volunteering among staff. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, its staff and the wider community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA its "15 Years+" Caring Organisation Logo for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA's sustainability strategy continues to adopt a structure comprising three pillars: environment, staff, and social responsibility. - Focus on decarbonisation and digitalisation of the HKMA's day-to-day operations, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 or before - Adopt green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines - Promote greener operational practices to the financial industry and wider society - Build a motivated workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA's strategic goals - Create a collaborative and inclusive working environment that values diversity and enhances staff belonging - Provide a quality working environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle - Foster a socially conscious culture - Incorporate social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management - Promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy through consumer education initiatives The HKMA takes climate change seriously and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced its plan to bring forward the target for achieving net-zero emissions from its institutional operations to 2030, which is 20 years ahead of its original commitment, as part of the Action Agenda. The HKMA has revised its roadmap towards net-zero transition, with a focus on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its day-to-day operations, concentrating on reducing carbon emissions, saving energy and reducing paper use, and recycling waste, while fully leveraging improvements in the fuel mix for electricity generation by local power companies. In addition, the HKMA has built a digitalised work environment to improve efficiency while simultaneously reducing its carbon footprint. Furthermore, recognising the importance of cultivating a culture of sustainability, the HKMA encourages staff to proactively adopt sustainable practices through the continued organisation of promotional programmes and activities. Under the primary 2030 net-zero target, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon-embedding tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and procuring with the lowest carbon footprint wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has been fully offsetting the carbon emissions from air travel through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel and participation in carbon offset programmes. The HKMA will expand its carbon-embedding and carbon-offset programmes to cover all other major carbon emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments in respect of actual operations, the HKMA continues to drive the low-carbon transition of the market, ranging from introducing electronic document submission and processing procedures to promoting electronic payments and collecting coins for recirculation. The remainder of this chapter sets out in more detail the HKMA's strategies in leading green efforts and promoting staff well-being and community care. Under the HKMA's overarching institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its day-to-day operations, including those arising from climate change. To better assess the potential operational impact of climate change, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and examined their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, the HKMA's offices are designed to incorporate measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans to incorporate comprehensive measures covering not only offices but also communications and computer facilities. The HKMA regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA also monitors its transition risks by tracking the greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption and paper usage arising from its own operations. The HKMA's latest climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 relating to its institutional operations by 2030 or before. These targets have been set with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology. The HKMA uses the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its institutional emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's principal greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions resulting from the consumption of fossil fuels to generate electricity. In the absence of data from individual suppliers, the HKMA takes a conservative approach in estimating its principal Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital goods) and services.
