Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculations for 2023 and 2024 are included in the Performance Summary on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA have been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and basis of verification are set out in the Verification Statement appended at the end of this report. The HKMA practises what it preaches, adhering to the same climate-related standards it expects of the banks it supervises and the financial system it oversees. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024, and will continue this effort in 2025 to achieve full green mobility. The HKMA continues to incorporate environmental considerations into the design, operation and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, during various renovation works in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and fitting materials or traded them in for new items at a discount to reduce waste. To improve overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and energy-saving measures for its offices and data centres, and adopted a modular uninterruptible power supply design in a 2024 data centre facility upgrade project to further optimise the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centre. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improved efficiency under partial load conditions, and is equipped with advanced cooling technology and higher power density, thereby helping to reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA enhances internal virtual collaboration through its digital workplace, complemented by streamlined workflows, which effectively reduces paper use. In addition, the HKMA extends the service life of mobile and desktop devices in line with manufacturers' software update cycles, allowing devices to be used safely for longer. To reduce waste generated in the office, the HKMA adheres to the "4R" principle of refuse, reduce, reuse and recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has placed recycling bins at multiple convenient locations in the office to collect different materials. To improve the recycling rate, the HKMA added recycling bins for drink cartons and plastic fruit mesh bags in 2024. In addition, since November 2022, the HKMA has been sending collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Event Waste Reduction Pledge", committing to taking measures to reduce waste generated at various events. The HKMA continues to prioritise procurement of goods meeting the environmental specifications of the government's "Green Procurement List", in particular electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their trips carefully, such as by consolidating multiple journeys when attending overseas events. At the institutional level, the HKMA has been purchasing sustainable aviation fuel since 2023 to reduce annual air travel carbon emissions by around 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in a Gold Standard-certified carbon offset programme to offset remaining air travel carbon emissions; this programme focuses on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as talks and tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance staff understanding of environmental sustainability issues. The HKMA held its inaugural "HKMA Green Month" from Earth Day on 22 April 2024 through the whole of May, themed "Think Green, Live Green, Work Green". This was an excellent opportunity for the HKMA to showcase its commitment and momentum in promoting environmental sustainability in its internal operations. Activities included a "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" encouraging staff to adopt green living practices, a "Save the Planet" quiz game, and a "Kokedama" indoor plant care workshop originating from Japan; waste audit results were also shared, and best practices for recycling were introduced by a community recycling centre operator. To sustain the momentum from "Green Month", the HKMA launched a recycling campaign of approximately six months' duration in October, highlighting responsible waste handling and reminding staff that small changes in individual habits can greatly improve the organisation's overall recycling performance. One highlight of the campaign was the release of a "Green Action" short video in which several senior staff members shared recycling tips. The campaign also featured a series of screensavers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles and electronic reminders to encourage staff to take action in reducing waste and increasing recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to gauge their awareness of sustainability and gather their views on proposed green office measures. The survey results will help inform future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong's de facto central banking institution, the HKMA sees itself as a key enabler of change, and therefore strives to lead the way in accelerating the low-carbon transition and encouraging the financial industry and the wider community to adopt sustainable practices. The HKMA has introduced a number of measures to improve the efficiency of external processes. Building on the successful launch of the Shared Data Submission Platform in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform's coverage in 2024 to include non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The purpose of expanding the platform's coverage is to further streamline the submission process for reporting entities and to provide a smoother experience for all users, while reinforcing the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new initiatives introduced in 2024 include a SurveyTool that allows banks to respond to HKMA questionnaires through a streamlined submission process, and an Intelligent Information and Document Management System, providing users with a centralised platform featuring advanced search capabilities for bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the "Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The Data covers total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and GHG emissions from air travel, as well as their respective intensities, for 2024. In addition, the Data also covers Scope 3 GHG emissions arising from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting for 2023 and 2024, along with their corresponding intensities. The HKMA's GHG emissions data was compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol) jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers a total of 6 office and warehouse asset, comprising 5 offices located at 1) Two International financial centres, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, and a warehouse at 6) Luk Cheung Industrial Centre, located in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 asset. The verification was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to provide a reasonable level of assurance for forming opinions and conclusions. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the Data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also examined the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checks, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the Data, and selecting representative data and information for review. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also subject to detailed review during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the Data. Our verification work was conducted with complete independence and impartiality. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: - The Data is materially accurate and reliable; - The overall data collection mechanism of the HKMA is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin, Verification Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2025
